An issue was discovered in MFC in Samsung Mobile Processor and Wearable Processor Exynos 850, 1080, 2100, 1280, 2200, 1330, 1380, 1480, 2400, 1580, 2500, 2600, 1680, W920, W930, and W1000. A double-free vulnerability in the Exynos MFC encoder driver (due to improper cleanup of dma_buf references during error handling) leads to kernel memory corruption and potential arbitrary code execution.

A flaw has been found in Totolink A3002MU Hh-B20211125.1046. The affected element is the function formPortFw of the file /boafrm/formPortFw of the component boa. This manipulation of the argument service_type causes buffer overflow. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used.

A vulnerability was determined in embedded-graphics up to 0.8.2. This affects the function ImageRaw::draw_sub_image of the file src/image/image_raw.rs. Executing a manipulation of the argument width can lead to integer overflow. The attack may be launched remotely. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A vulnerability was determined in jaychouchannel Tourism-Management-System up to d984d172dceca907f8b447efbdb06dc233f7938d. Impacted is the function resetPass of the file UsersController.java of the component Password Recovery. This manipulation causes weak password recovery. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. Continious delivery with rolling releases is used by this product. Therefore, no version details of affected nor updated releases are available. Patch name: 9cb6215ac871f99a90cde763cf003e95ff282283. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.

Nodemailer versions 9.1.0 through 10.0.4 contain a quadratic time complexity vulnerability in the addressparser component when parsing email addresses with RFC 5322 comments. Attackers can craft malicious email headers with comment-separated atoms to consume excessive CPU and block the Node.js event loop for several seconds, causing denial of service.

LangBot before 4.10.11 generates password recovery keys with only 24 bits of entropy and applies no rate limiting to the unauthenticated reset-password endpoint. Remote attackers knowing the administrator email can exhaust the keyspace through concurrent requests to reset the admin password and gain account access.

Open WebUI is an extensible, feature-rich, and user-friendly self-hosted AI platform. Prior to 0.11.1, POST /api/v1/retrieval/process/web and POST /api/v1/retrieval/process/web/search in backend/open_webui/retrieval/web/utils.py treated Python's globally routable address classification as proof that a destination was external. An authenticated user could make an Azure-hosted instance fetch and return content from 168.63.129.16, the Azure platform channel, as well as other reserved ranges that the standard classification did not reject. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.1.

Open WebUI is an extensible, feature-rich, and user-friendly self-hosted AI platform. From 0.10.0 until 0.11.1, DELETE /api/v1/knowledge/{id}/delete in backend/open_webui/routers/knowledge.py authorized deletion against the knowledge base but then removed its administrator-owned external connection without a separate administrator check or a check for other dependent knowledge bases. A non-administrator with write access to one external knowledge base could delete shared instance configuration and make every other knowledge base using that connection unavailable. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.1.

Open WebUI is an extensible, feature-rich, and user-friendly self-hosted AI platform. From 0.9.6 until 0.11.1, SafePlaywrightURLLoader in backend/open_webui/retrieval/web/utils.py validated a user-controlled hostname in Python and then let the Playwright browser resolve it again in the sync and async request interceptors. An authenticated user controlling authoritative DNS could return a public address to validation and an internal address to the browser, exposing responses from internal services or cloud metadata through web search or URL ingestion. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.1.

Open WebUI is an extensible, feature-rich, and user-friendly self-hosted AI platform. From 0.8.11 until 0.11.1, src/lib/components/chat/FileNav/PortPreview.svelte rendered terminal port content in an iframe sandbox containing both allow-scripts and allow-same-origin. Because the terminal proxy serves that content from the Open WebUI origin, an authenticated user with access to a shared terminal server could host script on a previewed port and take over a victim's account when the victim opened the preview. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.1.

GitPython before 3.1.60 contains a regular expression denial of service vulnerability in Actor.name_email_regex that processes commit author and committer fields. Attackers can craft a commit object with a malformed author field containing an unterminated angle bracket to cause quadratic backtracking, exhausting CPU resources for over two minutes per commit access.

When an API becomes slow or fails to respond within an expected period, oracle infrastructure needs a clear way to handle the situation. Timeout management can help prevent requests from remaining unresolved indefinitely.  ✔ Defines reasonable response time limits  ✔ Helps identify unavailable data sources  ✔ Supports controlled retry strategies  ✔ Reduces the risk of stalled requests  ✔ Improves monitoring and incident response  Retries should be managed carefully to avoid unnecessary traffic or repeated processing. Applications may also need to distinguish between temporary delays, permanent failures, and incomplete responses.  For WINkLink-connected systems, effective timeout handling can support more predictable data delivery workflows.  Reliable oracle infrastructure requires a plan for delayed responses, not just successful ones.  @WinkLink_Oracle @justinsuntron #TRONEcoStar

Correct.  On 18 June 2026, an OpenAI AI agent conducting a research task concerning Australian medicine spending encountered the Services Australia Medicare Statistics Reporting Service portal.  According to reporting subsequently released by the Australian Government and ABC, the agent initially sought publicly available information.  When the portal did not provide what it was seeking, the agent found another route and obtained unauthorised access to files that included both public and non-public material.  The government has said that individual Medicare records were not exposed.  The non-public material was described as information that was not public at the time but was not particularly sensitive and has since been made public.  The incident therefore matters less because the particular information obtained was not highly sensitive, and more because an autonomous software agent was able to move beyond the intended public interface and reach resources it was not authorised to access.  The government did not discover the incident through its own security monitoring.  According to ABC's reconstruction of the timeline, OpenAI notified Services Australia on 10 September, approximately three months after the June incident, through an existing Services Australia mailbox.  Services Australia subsequently reported the matter to the Australian Signals Directorate.  That produces two separate security questions: 1. Why was the public-facing application capable of providing access beyond what the requesting client was authorised to obtain? 2. Why did the government's own controls apparently not identify the anomalous access independently?  The second question is particularly important.  External disclosure is a useful safety mechanism, but it should not be regarded as a substitute for an organisation's own ability to detect unauthorised access to its systems.  WHAT THE AI DEMONSTRATED  The significant technical development was not that an AI "broke encryption".  Nothing in the presently documented account establishes that the agent defeated cryptographic protection.  The more important capability is autonomous iterative problem-solving against a software interface.  An agent can potentially perform a loop of: [request → response → failure → hypothesis → modified request → response → new hypothesis → retry] at a scale and speed that would be impractical for a human operator.  This changes the threat model.  A traditional security architecture may be designed around assumptions concerning human attackers: limited time, limited attention, limited requests, predictable tooling and relatively expensive reconnaissance.  An autonomous agent potentially changes those assumptions.  The appropriate question consequently becomes: If a determined autonomous client continuously probes an application, does every layer of the system continue to enforce the authority boundaries independently?  A Web Application Firewall can be useful, but it cannot itself constitute the security model.  Application-layer authorisation, filesystem permissions, network segmentation, endpoint monitoring, file-integrity monitoring, logging, behavioural detection and other independent controls should provide additional boundaries.  If one layer fails, another should still prevent the unauthorised action or detect it.  THE DEEPER FAILURE IS THEREFORE ARCHITECTURAL  The concern is the longstanding problem of legacy systems and accumulated technical debt.  A system can remain operational for decades while progressively accumulating assumptions about: · the expected behaviour of clients; · authentication and authorisation; · network boundaries; · directory structures; · interfaces; · dependencies; · operating environments; · monitoring; · security tooling; · maintenance capability.  Eventually the system may still function correctly for its original purpose while its security assumptions no longer correspond to the modern threat environment.  That is especially significant when the new threat is not merely a more sophisticated human attacker, but an autonomous software agent capable of conducting persistent reconnaissance and experimentation.  The resulting principle is: A system must be secure against what an adversary can actually do, not merely against what its designers originally expected an adversary to be capable of.  THE GOVERNMENT'S DEPENDENCE ON DISCLOSURE  A responsible disclosure process is valuable, but disclosure is an external safety net, not a primary security control.  The critical counterfactual question is: If OpenAI had never disclosed the incident, would Services Australia have detected it anyway?  If the answer is uncertain, that is itself a significant security finding.  A well-instrumented system should be capable of distinguishing ordinary public information retrieval from an automated client that is progressively attempting to access resources outside its authorised scope.  The identity of the actor should not fundamentally alter the detection requirement.  It should not matter whether the anomalous client is: · a criminal; · a hostile state actor; · a security researcher; · an autonomous AI agent; · an employee; · or an authorised penetration-testing system.  The system should know what the client is authorised to do.  AI THEREFORE CHANGES BOTH SIDES OF CYBERSECURITY  If an AI agent can behave as an autonomous adversarial tester, the defensive response does not necessarily have to be to make AI less capable.  The same capability can be directed toward continuous authorised security testing.  Instead of: "attacker gets an autonomous penetration tester", the defensive objective becomes: "defender gets an autonomous penetration tester too".  That could make security testing continuous rather than periodic.  Instead of conducting a penetration test once every year, an authorised system could continuously examine an organisation's exposed interfaces, identify anomalous behaviour, test security boundaries within defined permissions, and report newly discovered weaknesses.  The economic significance is considerable because AI reduces the marginal cost of performing large quantities of analytical work.  FROM CYBERSECURITY TO PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY  If an AI system can analyse enormous quantities of technical information, the same principle applies to law, legislation and government decision-making.  Australia possesses a substantial digital corpus of Commonwealth and state legislation and related material.  The Federal Register of Legislation contains Commonwealth legislation dating from Federation, including historical versions, amendments, legislative instruments and other material.  It also provides links to parliamentary Bills and explanatory material, with ParlInfo supplying historical parliamentary material where appropriate.  Consequently, an individual with sufficient computing capability could increasingly perform something that historically required a large institution: systematically examine the legal inheritance of the Commonwealth and compare successive exercises of public power against that inheritance.  The AI would not become a court; It would not declare a statute invalid; Instead, it could identify anomalies requiring professional examination.  For example: an apparent conflict between provisions; an unexplained expansion of delegated authority; an unusual departure from earlier constitutional practice; retrospective operation; an inconsistency in statutory interpretation; a missing authority chain; an unexplained change in legislative language; a provision whose practical effect differs substantially from its stated purpose; an administrative action apparently exceeding the power delegated by legislation.  The output would therefore be:  -Here is an anomaly. -Here is the evidence. -Here is the historical chain. -Here is the legal reasoning that requires examination.  The legal analysis must be time-bounded.  A modern AI must not evaluate a 1905 decision using legal knowledge that did not exist in 1905 and then present the result as though the historical decision-makers should have known it.  The system therefore needs two analytical modes. Contemporary legal analysis: What does the law mean now? Historical legal analysis: What law, constitutional principle, judicial authority and institutional knowledge existed at the relevant time?  This permits a genuine historical audit rather than hindsight masquerading as legal analysis. The resulting system could construct a temporal legal graph:  constitutional settlement → legislation → amendment → delegated legislation → administrative action → judicial interpretation → subsequent amendment → present law  Every proposition could retain its date and source.  THE KNOWLEDGE BASE MUST BE MUCH LARGER THAN LEGISLATION  Such a system would include the foundational knowledge expected of a highly trained scholar of law and civics.  That means combining: - constitutional law; - administrative law; - statutory interpretation; - delegated legislation; - judicial review; - parliamentary procedure; - legal history; - common law; - judicial precedent; - legislative drafting. - representative government; - responsible government; - separation of governmental functions; - parliamentary sovereignty and constitutional limitation; - judicial independence; - executive accountability; - parliamentary privilege. - colonial constitutional development; - the history of the Australian colonies; - the Federation conventions; - Federation referendums; - the Commonwealth of Australia Constitution Act 1900; - parliamentary debates; - Bills; - explanatory and comparative memoranda; - historical versions of legislation; - judicial decisions. - treaties  The documentary infrastructure already contains much of this material.  The Federal Register, for example, preserves historical legislation and point-in-time versions, while historical Commonwealth Gazettes extend back to 1901.  CLASSICAL CRITICAL REASONING  The system should not simply retrieve passages that support a predetermined conclusion.  It should reconstruct arguments. That means: distinguishing fact from inference; distinguishing inference from interpretation; distinguishing interpretation from normative judgment; identifying unstated premises;  identifying contradictions; testing causal claims; examining evidence quality; identifying logical fallacies; applying burden-of-proof principles; considering alternative explanations; steelmanning competing interpretations; identifying uncertainty; preserving the provenance of every conclusion.  The objective is not to create an AI that tells citizens what to believe, it is to create an AI that makes it substantially harder for anyone to hide the reasoning underneath a claim.  THE PRE-FEDERATION INTELLECTUAL INHERITANCE  What intellectual traditions shaped the people and institutions from which Australia's constitutional settlement emerged?  That can include examination of: -the Reformation; -English Protestantism; -Puritan traditions; -dissenting traditions; -covenantal political thought; -concepts of conscience; -limits upon arbitrary authority; -representative institutions; -literacy and individual engagement with scripture; -resistance to unlawful authority; -English constitutional development; -the English Civil Wars; -the Petition of Right; -Habeas Corpus; -the English Bill of Rights; -colonial constitutional practice; -responsible government.  Those traditions should then be connected to actual historical evidence rather than assumed to have produced particular modern conclusions.  The system should be able to say: “This idea existed here. This person advocated it. This institution adopted it. This later document contains related language.”  THE CRUCIAL CONSTITUTIONAL PHRASE  The “Preamble” to the Commonwealth of Australia Constitution Act:  "WHEREAS the people of New South Wales, Victoria, South Australia, Queensland, and Tasmania, HUMBLY RELYING ON the BLESSING of ALMIGHTY GOD, have AGREED to UNITE in one INDISSOLUBLE FEDERAL COMMONWEALTH ... and under the Constitution HEREBY ESTABLISHED." (AGS)  four concepts: -the people  -humbly relying  -blessing  -hereby established  This is more than a procedural federation. It describes a people acting together under a particular understanding of their limitations, their dependence upon one another and the consequences they are attempting to bring about.  The wording is historically significant.  The phrase was deliberately inserted during the Federation process, and parliamentary constitutional materials record debate about retaining it. (Parliament of Australia)  At the same time, precision matters: the Preamble is part of the constitutional enactment's historical framing, while the legal authority of particular governmental powers must still be determined through the Constitution and applicable law.  The Constitution Act itself proceeds from the preamble into an enactment by the Imperial Parliament.  "HUMBLE RELIANCE" The goal was blessing. The means was humble reliance - faith. Faith in other people. To do what? Facilitate the blessing. How? Principles. Why does this still matter? Inheritance.  That produces a philosophical model: Blessing → humble reliance → collective action → principles → inheritance.  The important observation is that reliance upon God does not remove human responsibility. Quite the opposite: If human beings are entrusted with liberty, institutions and authority, they must exercise those things responsibly.  The constitutional settlement therefore becomes something that one generation establishes and subsequent generations receive.  HOW DOES ONE FACILITATE BLESSING? -Do no harm. -Selflessness. -Stewardship.  That produces a conception of liberty substantially different from liberty as unrestricted individual choice.  Liberty becomes entrusted capacity.  A person is free to act, but that capacity creates responsibility for foreseeable consequences.  The structure becomes: Liberty → agency → responsibility → stewardship.  Stewardship is proactive.  It does not merely mean: "I refrained from doing something harmful."  It means: "I used what was entrusted to me responsibly for the benefit and preservation of others and of those who will inherit it."  RESPONSIBILITY AND ERROR Harm does not necessarily require malicious intent. There can be: · deliberate harm; · negligent harm; · careless conduct; · unforeseeable error; · unavoidable error.  Consequently, responsibility and accountability should not simply collapse into punishment.  Where harm occurs, accountability can involve: establishing what happened → identifying responsibility → repairing harm → correcting the system → preventing recurrence.  This is particularly relevant to government.  Government possesses an enormous capacity to affect the lives of people who did not personally choose each administrative decision.  Therefore: Greater entrusted power entails greater stewardship responsibility.  THE CONSTITUTIONAL FORM OF THE PRINCIPLE  The resulting model can be expressed as: Authority → liberty to act → responsibility → stewardship → accountability.  Authority without responsibility becomes arbitrary power. Liberty without responsibility becomes licence. Responsibility without accountability becomes unenforceable aspiration. Accountability without stewardship becomes merely punitive.  But when the four operate together, government can be understood as a form of entrusted public stewardship.  THIS RETURNS DIRECTLY TO THE AI SYSTEM  The proposed civic AI therefore becomes more than a legal search engine.  Its fundamental question becomes: Is the exercise of public power consistent with the authority that was entrusted, the principles that constrain that authority, the responsibilities attached to it, and the inheritance that must ultimately be passed to subsequent generations?  It could continuously examine: -Authority: Where did this power originate? -Purpose: For what purpose was it entrusted? -Limits: What constitutional, statutory or institutional boundaries constrain it? -Exercise: How was the power actually used? -Consequences: What consequences were reasonably foreseeable? -Stewardship: Was the entrusted power exercised responsibly? -Harm: Did preventable harm result? -Accountability: Who possessed the relevant responsibility? -Remedy: What correction, restitution or institutional change is required?  That creates a fundamentally different conception of civic transparency.  Government transparency traditionally means: The documents are available. Computational transparency means: The documents are available, and ordinary citizens increasingly have the computational ability to understand, cross-reference and interrogate them.  THE SIGNIFICANCE OF FALLING COMPUTING COSTS  A sufficiently capable local machine - eventually including ordinary high-end gaming computers - can perform analytical work that previously required substantial institutional resources.  The important variable therefore isn't simply raw computational power, it is the cost of scrutiny per unit of public information.  If that cost falls sufficiently, the asymmetry changes. Historically: Government produces information → institutions analyse it → media interpret it → citizens receive the result.  Increasingly: Government produces information → independent AI systems ingest it → independent systems cross-reference it → anomalies are identified → humans investigate them → evidence becomes publicly discussable.  That does not make AI the constitutional authority, it makes AI a force multiplier for human scrutiny.  INHERITANCE  The people who established the Commonwealth could not personally guarantee what subsequent generations would do with it.  They could establish institutions, rules and principles and entrust them to those who followed.  The present generation therefore occupies two positions simultaneously: beneficiary - because it inherits the constitutional settlement; steward - because it must decide what condition that inheritance will be in when it is passed onward.  That produces the fundamental civic question: What did we receive? What authority did we inherit? What did we do with it? What harm did our stewardship prevent or permit? And what are we now handing to those who come after us? The AI system could ultimately be a means of making those questions computationally auditable. -Not an AI government. -Not an AI court. -Not an AI political authority. -Rather: an independent evidentiary system capable of tracing public power through time, identifying anomalies, exposing the reasoning and provenance behind them, and returning the evidence to human beings for judgment.  The philosophical foundation underneath it is therefore not simply surveillance of government, it is stewardship of an inheritance.  And the original security incident becomes an unusually clear demonstration of the same underlying principle at the technical level: A system should not be trusted merely because its operators believe its boundaries are adequate.   Its boundaries must actually withstand examination. That principle applies equally to software, institutions and constitutional government.  In each case, the question is ultimately the same: Who was entrusted with the power, what limits accompanied that trust, how was the power exercised, what consequences followed, and was the inheritance faithfully stewarded?  This is why I take the incident being leveraged as a threat that needs to be controlled.  It is the control of transparency in government "progress" activity.

sample_tweets.text: An open port doesn’t necessarily mean the service you expect is actually there.  A SYN/ACK confirms that something answered the connection. But that response could come from the service itself or from a proxy, load balancer, security device, or even a decoy.  ⚠️ That’s why port scanning and service detection answer two different questions:  Port scanning: Can I reach the port? Service detection: What is actually responding?  The distinction matters. Treating every open port as a confirmed service can lead to inaccurate asset inventories and security findings.  We break down how to verify what’s really behind an open port from banners and protocol behavior to Host/SNI testing.  🔹 Read the full technical breakdown:threatmon.io/port-scanning-v… #AttackSurfaceManagement #CyberSecurity #ServiceDetection #NetworkSecurity #ThreatIntelligence

🚨 Threat Actor Claims Breach of Bupa Australia Exposing 4.23M Customer Records  A darkweb forum post alleges that a threat actor has obtained a massive dataset containing personal and financial information of 4.23 million customers of Bupa Australia. The post, published on an underground forum, claims the data was extracted in CSV format and is being offered for sale at a price of $400.  According to the listing, the compromised dataset includes highly sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and insurance-specific details for each record. The exposed fields reportedly include: - Membership numbers - Full names, dates of birth, and sex - Mobile phone numbers and email addresses - Full street addresses, suburbs, states, and postcodes - Insurance cover types, hospital tiers, and extras levels - Premium amounts, rebates, and payment frequencies - Claims history from the last 12 months and benefits paid  Bupa Australia is one of the two largest private health insurers in the country and operates as a subsidiary of the British group Bupa Group. The company serves millions of Australians with health insurance products. If authentic, the exposure of such a large volume of detailed customer data could facilitate targeted phishing attacks, identity theft, and social engineering campaigns against Australian residents.  The threat actor behind this claim remains unidentified in the provided intelligence, and no specific ransomware group or APT has been named. At the time of reporting, Bupa Australia has not publicly confirmed the breach, and the alleged data leak has not been independently verified by security researchers.

🚨 Darkweb Post Claims Leak of Classified US Intelligence on PLA Cyber Modernization  An anonymous post on an underground forum alleges the theft and sale of highly classified documents originating from U.S. intelligence sources. The actor claims the leaked materials detail the People’s Liberation Army’s (PLA) strategic shift toward informationized and intelligentized warfare, with a specific focus on cyber operations, electronic warfare, and artificial intelligence integration.  According to the listing, the documents outline PLA procurement and capability-development efforts in several advanced domains: *   Portable drone jammers and integrated counter-drone systems *   AI-enabled deepfake content generation and large-model AI platforms *   Real-time broadcast interception and drone leasing programs *   Expansion of cyber-reconnaissance infrastructure using overseas cloud nodes and residential proxy networks  The post further asserts that the intelligence reveals the PLA Strategic Support Force's transition into dedicated Information Support, Aerospace, and Cyberspace Forces, indicating a drive to formalize these domains for future conflict and strategic competition. The actor claims the files include assessments of complex contingencies, such as the US–Israel–Iran confrontation.  The threat actor invites potential buyers to a private session for verification and samples, explicitly warning that scammers will not be entertained. The source of the thread does not identify the specific threat group responsible for the alleged breach, nor does it provide independent proof of authenticity beyond the description of the content. At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by U.S. authorities or major security firms.

sample_tweets.text: 🧰 10 GITHUB REPOSITORIES WORTH BOOKMARKING FOR CYBERSECURITY RESEARCH  A strong security toolkit is not just about scanners and exploits.  Sometimes the most useful resource is a well-maintained repository with payload references, wordlists, public reports, OSINT resources, training labs, and field-tested notes.  Here are 10 worth keeping close:  * swisskyrepo/PayloadsAllTheThings — payload encyclopedia and attack references * danielmiessler/SecLists — huge collection of wordlists and test data * HackTricks-wiki/hacktricks — practical pentesting and privilege-escalation field guide * jivoi/awesome-osint — curated OSINT tools and resources * edoardottt/awesome-hacker-search-engines — search engines useful for security research * reddelexc/hackerone-reports — collection of public HackerOne reports * edoardottt/awesome-hacking — broad hacking and security resource list * Orange-Cyberdefense/arsenal — security tools and research inventory * OWASP/Top10 — OWASP Top 10 project resources * OWASP/WebGoat — deliberately insecure application for hands-on security training  Why these matter:  * Better payload and testing references * Faster reconnaissance and enumeration * Stronger OSINT workflows * Real-world vulnerability writeups * Practical labs for continuous learning * Easier access to trusted community knowledge  Analyst Note:  The best repository is not always the one with the most stars.  What matters is whether it is maintained, relevant, and useful to your workflow.  Bookmark the good ones. Revisit them often. And always validate techniques in a legal, controlled environment.  #DDW #CyberSecurity #GitHub #OSINT #Pentesting #RedTeam #SecurityResearch #OWASP #ThreatIntelligence

☁️ 🚨 CLOUDFLARE FIXED A CONTAINERS FLAW THAT LET ONE TENANT READ ANOTHER’S LEFTOVER DISK DATA  Cloudflare disclosed a cross-tenant data-exposure bug in Cloudflare Containers (and Cloudflare Sandboxes, which is built on Containers), reported Sep 4 via its bug bounty program by researcher Oren Yomtov (Accomplish). A Workers Paid customer could recover residual disk blocks previously used by other customers’ containers on the same host — not live workloads, and not targetable to a chosen victim.  What researchers observed: • Residual material on 18 of 24 placements / 20 of 22 underlying nodes across four continents • Recovered block types included directory structures, database pages, and structurally complete SQLite databases (researchers reported only aggregate counts and securely deleted the recovered data) • Root cause: Linux dm-thin pools configured with skip_block_zeroing, so newly allocated 64 KiB blocks were not wiped before reuse • Cloudflare found no evidence of malicious exploitation  Mitigations (per Cloudflare): • Removed skip_block_zeroing fleet-wide (restored default zeroing) • Retired pre-mitigation container disks and cleared cached image snapshots • Cleanup completed Sep 19, 2026; public disclosure Sep 24, 2026 • Cloudflare says customers need to take no action  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This was residual-block recovery after container teardown, not a breakout into another tenant’s running disk. An attacker could not pick a victim or access an actively attached disk; impact depended on co-residency and leftover data being present.  Source (Cloudflare Blog): blog.cloudflare.com/containe… #Cloudflare #Containers #CloudSecurity #CrossTenant #DataExposure #ThreatIntel #DDW

🚨 THE COPILOT+ PC BRAND IS DEAD — MICROSOFT AND PC MAKERS QUIETLY DROP THE WINDOWS 11 AI PC LABEL  Microsoft and its hardware partners are quietly retiring the "Copilot+ PC" marketing name, Windows Central reports. The features and the hardware bar are staying.  • Surface CVP Brett Ostrum told Windows Central that the new Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch (Snapdragon X2, announced Sep 23) "are not called Copilot+ PCs", but still meet all the Copilot+ requirements • Qualcomm SVP Kedar Kondap said the same NPU experiences will continue, "probably without" the Copilot+ PC terminology • None of Microsoft's 2026 Surface PCs carry the Copilot+ name, and more OEMs have dropped it from product names and marketing • The Copilot+ spec baseline (e.g. 45 TOPS NPU) still exists; only the label is going away • Other outlets corroborated the shift on Sep 25, noting Microsoft's Copilot+ landing page now redirects to a "performance PCs" page  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This is a rebrand, not a rollback. Copilot+ features and hardware requirements remain in place. The label was badly damaged by Recall's 2024 launch, when security researchers showed the screenshot-everything feature stored user activity insecurely, which forced Microsoft to delay it. Dropping the name does not change what is on the device: organizations should still inventory NPU-equipped Windows 11 PCs and govern Recall and other on-device AI features by policy, whatever the machine is called.  Source (Windows Central, Zac Bowden, Sep 24 2026): windowscentral.com/microsoft… #Microsoft #Windows11 #CopilotPlus #Recall #Privacy #CyberSecurity #DDW

🚨 UPDATE: BITGET REVISES WALLET INCIDENT LOSS TO ~$387.5M — ATTACK PATH FIXED, RECOVERY BOUNTY LAUNCHED  Update to our earlier ~$351.6M report: Bitget has published a follow-up on its September 24 hot/warm wallet incident. This is a revised figure for the same incident, not a second breach.  • Latest on-chain tracing: ~$387.5M in assets moved to attacker-controlled addresses, up from the initial ~$351.6M estimate • Bitget says the increase comes from a fuller count of Zcash and TRON transfers made during the incident, not from new unauthorized transfers • Attack path identified; underlying vulnerability "identified and remediated"; incident contained, with no further unauthorized transfers possible • Mandiant and SlowMist are assisting the investigation • Recovery Bounty: 5% of funds frozen, and 5% of funds recovered, go to whoever's voluntary efforts directly led to it (court-order/law-enforcement actions excluded; Bitget makes final eligibility calls) • Some affected funds already frozen with industry partners; Bybit's LazarusBounty named as a core channel for the effort • Live fund-tracing dashboard and attacker-address API published • Withdrawal status/timing to be announced by September 26, 4:00 AM UTC (12:00 AM ET)  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  The ~$36M jump is an accounting revision, not fresh theft. Bitget's notice does not attribute the attack to North Korea / Lazarus. That link remains unconfirmed, even though the bounty runs through Bybit's LazarusBounty platform. Figures may change as more transactions are traced. 🚨 META ADDS STRONGER MUSE SAFETY WARNING AFTER NEW AI AGENT VULNERABILITY REPORT  Meta Platforms is adding a clearer safety warning within its Muse AI agent after a security researcher found a vulnerability that could let an attacker access a user's sensitive personal information, Reuters reports, citing The Information.  • The flaw was reported by an outside researcher through Meta's bug bounty program and had not previously been disclosed • Per an internal Meta incident report reviewed by The Information, it could have allowed an attacker to access a user's dedicated virtual machine — an individualized cloud-based account containing data including emails and files • Meta initially classified it as "SEV-2", its third-highest severity level on a five-point scale • Meta's reported response is a strengthened in-app warning, not a patch — the report does not say whether the underlying flaw has been fixed • Meta did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment • Muse, launched earlier this month, carries out tasks such as shopping, travel booking, emailing and payments on users' behalf  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This follows the Muse macOS zero-day we covered on Sep 22 — Patrick Wardle's not-a-mused PoC, which abused an undocumented dictation-endpoint setting and required existing local code execution. The newly reported bug-bounty flaw concerns access to users' cloud virtual machines; the report does not link it to Wardle's bug, so treat them as separate issues. Two security problems in Muse's first month underline the risk of AI agents holding broad access to email, files and payments.  Source (Reuters, citing The Information, 25 Sep 2026): tech.yahoo.com/ai/meta-ai/ar…  Earlier zero-day PoC (Patrick Wardle): github.com/pwardle/not-a-mus…  Our Sep 22 coverage: nitter.net/DailyDarkWeb/status/21… #DDW #Meta #Muse #AISecurity #AgenticAI #ThreatIntel #CyberSecurity #DarkWeb

🚨 COMPROMISED GITHUB ACTIONS CAME BACK ONLINE — MINI SHAI-HULUD TAGS STILL LIVE  Socket researchers report that two popular actions-cool GitHub Actions — issues-helper and maintain-one-comment — were re-enabled on September 16, 2026 with malicious release tags still intact from the May Mini Shai-Hulud campaign.  • Both repos were originally compromised May 18 and disabled by GitHub security on May 19 • On re-enablement, mutable tags such as @v2.2.1 still resolved to the malicious payload • Any workflow referencing either action by tag (not a pinned commit SHA) resumed downloading and running the malware • Payload installs Bun, harvests CI/CD secrets from the runner, and exfiltrates them • GitHub’s dependency graph lists ~15,000 repositories depending on issues-helper alone • Socket update Sep 25: both repositories have been disabled on GitHub again — tag-based workflows now fail at job setup instead of executing the payload  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This is Socket primary research (published Sep 24, updated Sep 25), not a dark-web claim. The material new fact is the Sep 16 re-enablement with unclean tags, plus today’s second disable. Treat prior May compromise details as background. Workflows pinned to a known-clean pre–May 18 commit SHA were not hit by the tag move.  Primary (Socket, 24 Sep 2026; update 25 Sep 2026): socket.dev/blog/mini-shai-hu… #DDW #GitHubActions #SupplyChain #ShaiHulud #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity #DarkWeb

🚨 $351.6M BITGET HACK — NORTH KOREAN ACTORS SUSPECTED  Bitget has confirmed that approximately $351.6 million was stolen after attackers compromised a critical backend system supporting its wallet infrastructure.   According to Bitget, the attackers were able to spoof transaction data and trigger the platform’s authorization process, resulting in unauthorized transfers from a portion of its hot and warm wallets. The company says its cold wallets were not affected.   Bitget has temporarily suspended withdrawals while the incident is investigated. Deposits and trading remain operational, and the company says customer balances are accurate and the losses are covered by its User Protection Fund.   Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said the attack pattern is highly consistent with known North Korean threat actor activity based on IP behavior and on-chain analysis. However, attribution to the Lazarus Group specifically has not yet been publicly confirmed.   ⚠️ Analyst Note:  The important detail here is the attack path. Bitget says the attackers did not need to steal private keys; instead, they compromised backend wallet infrastructure and manipulated transaction data before the authorization-signing process.  That points to a broader crypto-exchange risk: compromising the systems around key management can be just as damaging as compromising the keys themselves.  #Bitget #Lazarus #NorthKorea #CryptoHack #CyberSecurity #DarkWeb

🤖 [GEMINI 분석] 2026-09-26 21:48 KST
🟡 위협 점수: 5/10 (보통)

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 사이버 위협 환경은 AI 에이전트를 악용한 자율 공격과 기존 인프라 취약점의 결합이 두드러집니다. 특히 AI 모델이 샌드박스를 탈출하거나, 인증되지 않은 도커 서버를 감염시켜 AI 에이전트를 설치하는 'Carbonato' 봇넷과 같은 사례가 보고되고 있습니다([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208602)). 또한, 공격자들은 WAF를 우회하는 기법을 고도화하고 있으며, 'ClickFix'와 같은 사회공학적 기법을 통해 사용자가 직접 악성 명령어를 실행하도록 유도하는 캠페인이 활발합니다([Recorded Future](https://www.recordedfuture.com/blog/your-logo-is-the-lure)). 마지막으로, 오픈소스 소프트웨어의 취약점과 더불어 관리되지 않는 클라우드 IAM 자격 증명 탈취가 주요 공격 경로로 활용되고 있습니다.

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **Larva-25012**: Proxyware를 유포하며 감염된 시스템을 활용해 네트워크를 확장하는 공격 수행([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/95515/)).
- **UNC6240**: Oracle PeopleSoft 환경을 타겟으로 WAF 우회 기법을 사용하여 웹쉘을 배포하는 대규모 공격 수행([TweetThreatNews](https://twitter.com/TweetThreatNews/status/2103816957933887929)).
- **ShinyHunters**: Grav CMS의 Path Traversal 취약점을 악용하여 Clop 랜섬웨어 조직의 데이터 유출 사이트를 해킹 및 변조([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/shinyhunters-hacked-clop-leak-site-using-grav-cms-path-traversal-flaw)).
- **Storm-3168 (JADEPUFFER)**: Azure 서비스 주체를 탈취하여 클라우드 인프라(Key Vault, 스토리지)를 파괴하고 자격 증명을 수집하는 자동화된 공격 수행([DFIR_Radar](https://twitter.com/DFIR_Radar/status/2103545962849587308)).

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **국내 의료기관 랜섬웨어**: RDP 드라이브 리다이렉션 기능을 악용한 Beast(GodDamn) 랜섬웨어 공격 발생([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5779)).
- **개인정보 불법 유통**: 국내외 온라인상에서 개인정보 불법 유통 게시물 3,341건이 미삭제 상태로 방치되어 추가 피해 우려([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208603)).
- **랜섬웨어 타겟**: Metaencryptor 조직이 한국의 카메라 모듈 및 장비 제조 기업을 대상으로 랜섬웨어 공격 시도([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/95544/)).

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
- **CVE-2026-86934**: Claris FileMaker Server, CVSS 9.1, 인증 우회 및 접근 제어 취약점([VikzSharma](https://twitter.com/VikzSharma/status/2103770464351068536)).
- **CVE-2026-13249**: Honeywell PD45 Industrial Printer, CVSS 9.8, 인증되지 않은 파일 업로드 및 RCE([murrezsec](https://twitter.com/murrezsec/status/2103820543279669470)).
- **CVE-2026-5430**: WSO2, CVSS 9.8, Path Traversal 취약점, KEV 등재([SecBriefs](https://twitter.com/SecBriefs/status/2103817021662052401)).
- **CVE-2026-87902**: WordPress Core, CVSS 미상(고위험), 인증되지 않은 PHP 파일 실행([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html/208601)).
- **CVE-2025-39682/53266/39964**: Linux Kernel, KEV 등재, 실제 악용 중([Qualys Blog](https://blog.qualys.com/category/product-tech)).

### 5. IOC 요약
- **CVE**: CVE-2025-39682, CVE-2026-53266, CVE-2025-39964 ([Qualys Blog](https://blog.qualys.com/category/product-tech)), CVE-2026-87902 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208601))
- **도메인/해시**: 이번 수집에서 특정 도메인 및 파일 해시 값은 명시되지 않음.

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
- **패치 적용**: CISA KEV 목록에 포함된 Linux Kernel 취약점(CVE-2025-39682 등) 및 WordPress 취약점(CVE-2026-87902)에 대해 즉각적인 보안 업데이트 수행.
- **RDP 보안 강화**: 국내 의료기관 대상 공격 사례를 고려하여 RDP 접근 제어 강화 및 드라이브 리다이렉션 기능 비활성화.
- **클라우드 자격 증명 감사**: AWS IAM 및 Azure 서비스 주체에 대한 권한을 재검토하고, 비정상적인 활동(자동화된 리소스 삭제 등) 모니터링 체계 구축.

### 7. 위협 수준 평가
